metadata.direction_rule: Tractability is scored in the direction the signature wants. Complement components, Fc receptors and cytokines must go DOWN and are reached by antibodies and biologics rather than small molecules, so they score low. Complement regulators (CD55, CD59), the inhibitory receptor FCGR2B, IL10, FOXP3 and the myelin genes must go UP and have no small-molecule route, so they score lower still.
metadata.purpose: Per-target modality annotation for Guillain-Barre syndrome. Tells the design layer which proteins a small molecule can realistically engage.

schema.small_molecule_tractability: 0-1 ordinal prior that a drug-like small molecule can productively engage this protein; 0 marks a transcriptional readout rather than a target
schema.note: the reason for the value, so it can be argued with

metadata.curation_rule: Ordinal priors reflecting precedent in the public literature, on the same scale as the MS, Parkinson's, Alzheimer's and epilepsy annotations. Judgements, not measurements.
metadata.readout_convention: A target scoring below 0.2 is treated by the design engine as a readout: the profile may require its expression to move, but no arm of a designed molecule will be assigned to bind it.
metadata.the_defining_problem: Guillain-Barre syndrome is the disease whose established treatments are not small molecules at all. Intravenous immunoglobulin and plasma exchange are biologic and procedural, and the newer candidates are antibodies and enzymes against complement, IgG and FcRn. The central pathogenic targets (C1q, C5, IgG, FcRn) score 0.05 to 0.2 for small-molecule tractability, so a small-molecule design has to work around the disease's own centre of gravity, through targets on its edges: the C5a receptor, sodium channels for pain, SARM1 for axon protection, glucosylceramide synthase for the ganglioside substrate, and Kv1.1 for conduction.

B4GALNT1.note: Ganglioside synthase; inhibitors are tool compounds

C1QA.note: Classical-pathway recognition subunit; reached by antibodies (tanruprubart), with few small molecules

C1S.note: Serine protease with small-molecule inhibitors in development

C3.note: Complement hub; peptide inhibitors (compstatin class) dominate

C5.note: Reached by antibodies (eculizumab) and a macrocyclic peptide; small molecules are rare

C5AR1.note: Avacopan is an approved small-molecule antagonist

CACNA2D1.note: Alpha-2-delta-1; gabapentin and pregabalin bind it

CCL2.note: A chemokine, reached through its receptor

CD55.note: Decay-accelerating factor; raising a complement regulator is not a small-molecule goal

CD59.note: Membrane-attack-complex inhibitor; raising it is not a small-molecule goal

CNTN1.note: Contactin-1, a paranodal readout and an autoantibody target

EGR2.note: Schwann-cell myelination transcription factor; induced, not bound

FCGR1A.note: High-affinity IgG receptor; antibody and IVIG blockade, few small molecules

FCGR2A.note: Low-affinity IgG receptor; blocked by antibodies

FCGR2B.note: Inhibitory IgG receptor, whose raising is the wanted direction and has no small-molecule route

FCGR3A.note: IgG receptor on macrophages and NK cells; blocked by antibodies

FCGRT.note: FcRn; blocked by antibody fragments (efgartigimod); small-molecule FcRn blockers are early

FOXP3.note: Regulatory T-cell transcription factor; raising it is not a small-molecule goal

GDNF.note: A growth factor; delivered or induced

GJB1.note: Connexin 32; raising it has no small-molecule route

HMOX1.note: An inducible compensatory response, raised by upstream Nrf2 activation rather than bound

ICAM1.note: Adhesion molecule; antibody and peptide blockers

IFNG.note: A cytokine; reached through upstream signalling

IGHG1.note: Immunoglobulin heavy chain, a readout of IgG deposition

IL10.note: Raising an anti-inflammatory cytokine is the wanted direction and has no small-molecule route

IL17A.note: Antibodies dominate; oral small molecules are early

IL1B.note: Reached through the inflammasome or receptor antagonism

IL6.note: A cytokine, reached by antibodies and JAK inhibitors upstream

ITGAM.note: Integrin alpha-M; antibodies and small-molecule modulators are early

JUN.note: Regeneration-associated transcription factor; induced, not bound

KCNA1.note: Kv1.1 exposed by demyelination; dalfampridine blocks it, and blocking is the wanted direction

MMP9.note: Metalloprotease with hydroxamate and non-zinc inhibitors

MPZ.note: Myelin protein zero, a myelin-integrity readout

MS4A1.note: CD20, reached by antibodies; not a small-molecule target

MYD88.note: Adaptor; inhibitors are peptidomimetic tool compounds

NEFL.note: Neurofilament light, the axonal-injury biomarker, a readout

NFASC.note: Neurofascin 155, a paranodal readout and an autoantibody target

NFKB1.note: Transcription factor; reached through upstream kinases

NGF.note: A growth factor; delivered or induced

NMNAT2.note: Axon-survival enzyme; raising it is wanted, and activators are unusual

NRG1.note: Axonal signal driving myelination; delivered or induced, not bound

S1PR1.note: Fingolimod and the newer S1P modulators act through functional antagonism

SARM1.note: NADase driving axon degeneration, with small-molecule inhibitors reported

SCN8A.note: Nav1.6 at the node; restoration is wanted, and activators are scarce

SCN9A.note: Nav1.7; the target of selective aryl-sulfonamide and newer inhibitors

SOD2.note: Antioxidant enzyme, induced rather than bound

TRPV1.note: Antagonists and desensitising agonists are well-precedented

UGCG.note: Glucosylceramide synthase; eliglustat is an approved inhibitor

VCAM1.note: Adhesion molecule; reached through VLA-4 blockade

VEGFA.note: A growth factor, reached by antibodies and receptor kinase inhibitors
